verses.text: This the divine drop from Jesus, straight from the Father, coded to show his crew what’s about to go down, fast. He sent it through his angel to his guy John, who’s locked in.
John posted the full download—God’s Word, Jesus’ receipts, and everything he saw with his own eyes.
Big ups to the one who reads this scroll out loud, and to the squad who taps in and keeps it tight. Clock’s ticking.
From John, to the seven church squads in Asia: Grace and peace from the One who was, is, and still pulling up, and from the seven Spirits vibing at the throne.
And from Jesus Christ—the realest witness, first to beat death, and top boss of all kings. He loves us deep and dropped his blood to free us from our mess.
He leveled us up—made us royalty and priests for his Dad. All glory and power to him forever. No cap. Amen.
Look—he’s pulling up in the clouds, and everybody gonna see him, even the ones who did him dirty. Whole world gonna be shook. Facts.
“I’m Alpha and Omega,” says the Lord God. “I’m the start, the now, and the always. I got this on lock.”
I’m John, your bro in the trenches, catching heat and holding the line for Jesus. I was vibing solo on Patmos island for preaching and repping God’s Word.
I was in full Spirit mode on the Lord’s Day, when I heard a voice behind me—loud like a bass drop.
It said, “Yo, write this down in a scroll and send it to the seven churches: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”
I spun around to peep the voice, and saw seven golden lampstands.
In the middle of the lamp squad was someone looking like the Son of Man, dripped in a long robe with a gold belt flexing on his chest.
His hair was white like snow, fresh and clean. Eyes? Straight fire emojis (but real).
Feet? Glowing like metal fresh out the forge. Voice? Ocean-level thunder.
He had seven stars in his right hand, and a sharp double-edged sword coming from his mouth. His face? Bright —like staring at the sun in full blast.
I dropped like I got KO’d. But he touched me and said, “Don’t trip. I’m the First and the Last.”
“I’m the one who died—but look, I’m alive forever. I got the keys to death and the underworld. I run this.”
“So jot this down: what you’ve seen, what’s happening now, and what’s coming next.”
“Here’s the cheat code for the seven stars you saw in my hand and the seven lampstands: the stars = angels of the seven churches, and the lampstands = the churches themselves.”
To the messenger of the Ephesus crew: Write this— The one holding the seven stars, walking through the golden lamp squad, says:
I see your grind. You don’t clock out. You don’t mess with frauds. You tested fake apostles and exposed the cap. Respect.
You’ve been holding it down, taking hits for my name, and you didn’t fold.
But I got beef with you—you ghosted your first love.
Run it back. Remember where you fell off. Switch it up. Do what you did at first. If not, I’m pulling up and snatching your lampstand. No bluff.
But hey—you do hate the Nicolaitans’ mess, and I hate it too.
Got ears? Then listen to what the Spirit’s saying to the churches. To the ones who make it through, I’ll let you eat from the Tree of Life, chilling in God’s paradise.
To the messenger of the Smyrna squad: Write this— The First and the Last, who died and came back, says:
I know your struggle. I see the broke vibes—but you’re actually rich. I see the slander from those fake Jews, repping the synagogue of Satan.

Don’t flinch at what’s coming. The devil’s about to throw some of y’all in lockdown to test you. You’ll catch ten days of heat. Stay loyal, even if it costs your life, and I’ll crown you with forever life.
Got ears? Then hear what the Spirit’s saying to the churches. The ones who make it? Death 2.0 can’t touch them.
To the messenger of the Pergamos crew: Write this— The one with the sharp double-edged sword says:
I know where you live—Satan’s got a whole throne there. Still, you’re repping my name. You didn’t fold, even when Antipas, my loyal witness, got murked in your zone—Satan’s turf.
But I got a few things against you. Some of y’all are riding with Balaam’s playbook—dude who coached Balak to trip up Israel, get them to eat idol food and wild out.
Same way, you got folks vibing with the Nicolaitan crew. That ain’t it.
So switch it up, or I’m pulling up fast and clapping back with the sword from my mouth.
Got ears? Then hear what the Spirit’s saying to the churches. The ones who make it? I’ll drop that hidden manna. I’ll give them a white stone with a new name on it—only they’ll know what it says.
To the messenger of the Thyatira squad: Write this— The Son of God, eyes blazing and feet like molten metal, says:
I see your love, your grind, your faith, your service, your patience. You’re doing more now than you did before. Leveling up.
But I got smoke with you. You’re letting that Jezebel chick run wild—calls herself a prophet, but she’s leading my people into hookup culture and idol feasts.
I gave her time to chill and turn around, but she’s not about that repentance life.
So I’m throwing her on a sickbed. Her crew? If they don’t bounce from her mess, they’re going down with her.
I’ll strike her followers dead. Then all the churches will know I’m the one who scans hearts and minds. I’ll pay everyone back based on their moves.
But to the rest of y’all in Thyatira, who didn’t mess with her chaos or dive into “deep Satan stuff” (as they call it)—I’m not dropping any extra weight on you.
Just hold tight to what you got till I show up.
The one who conquers and stays loyal to the end? I’ll give them power over nations.
They’ll rule with iron vibes, smashing like pottery. Just like I got that authority from my Dad.
And I’ll hand them the morning star.
Got ears? Then hear what the Spirit’s saying to the churches.
To the messenger of the Sardis squad: Write this— The one with the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars says: I see your rep—you got the name like you’re alive, but you’re spiritually flatlined.
Wake up. Lock in. What’s left is barely hanging on. I checked your works—they’re not hitting God’s standard.
So run it back. Remember what you got and how you got it. Hold tight. Flip the switch. If you don’t, I’m pulling up like a thief—no heads-up.
But you got a few real ones in Sardis who didn’t stain their fits. They’ll walk with me in white—‘cause they earned it.
The one who makes it through? I’ll deck them out in white drip. I won’t blot their name from the Book of Life. I’ll shout them out in front of my Father and his angels.
Got ears? Then hear what the Spirit’s saying to the churches.
To the messenger of the Philadelphia crew: Write this— The Holy One, the True One, the Key-of-David holder, who opens what no one can shut and shuts what no one can open, says:
I know your grind. I dropped an open door in front of you—no one can close it. You’ve got little strength, but you kept my word and didn’t ghost my name.
I’ll make the fake Jews—the ones from Satan’s clique—pull up and bow at your feet. They’ll know I’m rocking with you.
Since you kept my “hold on” command, I’ll keep you safe from the global test that’s coming to shake the whole planet.
I’m pulling up fast. Hold tight to what you got, so no one swipes your crown.
The one who makes it? I’ll make them a pillar in God’s house—never leaving. I’ll tag them with God’s name, the name of God’s city (New Jerusalem, coming down from heaven), and my new name too.
Got ears? Then hear what the Spirit’s saying to the churches.
To the messenger of the Laodicea squad: Write this— The Amen, the faithful and true witness, the OG of God’s creation, says:
I know your moves. You’re not hot or cold. I wish you were one or the other.
But since you’re just mid—lukewarm—I’m about to spit you out.
You say, “I’m rich, I got it all, I don’t need anything.” But you don’t even see it—you’re broke, busted, blind, and spiritually naked.
I’m telling you: cop gold from me, refined in fire, so you can actually be rich. Get white fits to cover your shame. And eye drops so you can finally see.
I call out and check the ones I love. So get serious. Flip the switch.
Look—I’m at the door, knocking. If anyone hears and opens up, I’ll come through, eat with them, and vibe together.
The one who makes it? I’ll let them sit with me on my throne—just like I made it and sat with my Dad on his.
Got ears? Then hear what the Spirit’s saying to the churches.
After that, I looked up—and boom, a door wide open in the sky. The same voice I heard earlier, loud like a trumpet, said, “Pull up here. I’ll show you what’s next on the rollout.”
Instantly, I was in Spirit mode. And there it was—a throne in heaven, and someone sitting on it.
The one on the throne? Shining like jasper and sardine stone. Whole vibe glowing, with a rainbow aura that looked like emerald drip.
Around the throne were twenty-four other thrones, and on them sat twenty-four elders, dressed in white fits, rocking gold crowns like royalty.
Lightning cracked out from the throne—booms and rumbles everywhere. Seven blazing torches were lit in front of it—those are the seven Spirits of God.
In front of the throne was something like a glass sea—clear like crystal. Right around the throne, on all sides, were four living beings, full of eyes front and back. No blind spots.
First creature? Lion-coded. Second? Straight up ox energy. Third had a human face. Fourth? Flying eagle vibes.

Each of the four had six wings, eyes everywhere—even under the wings. And they never clocked out, day or night, always saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, who is, and who’s still pulling up.”
Every time the creatures drop glory, honor, and thanks to the One on the throne—the Eternal One—
the twenty-four elders fall flat, worshipping the One who lives forever. They toss their crowns at the throne, saying:
“You’re worthy, Lord. All the glory, honor, and power’s yours. You built everything. It all exists ‘cause you wanted it to.”
Then I peeped the One on the throne holding a scroll—written front and back, sealed tight with seven locks.
And I saw this massive angel, voice booming: “Who’s worthy to crack the seals and open this scroll?”
But no one—up top, down here, or under the dirt—could even step up to open it or peek inside.
I started tearing up heavy, ‘cause no one was worthy to unlock the scroll or even glance at it.
Then one of the elders told me, “Chill. Stop crying. Look—the Lion from Judah’s tribe, the Root of David, just secured the W. He’s got what it takes to break the seals and open the scroll.”
I looked again, and there he was—a Lamb, standing like he’d been through it. He had seven horns and seven eyes (aka the seven Spirits of God sent everywhere).
The Lamb stepped up and took the scroll right outta the hand of the One on the throne.
When he grabbed it, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders dropped to their knees before him. Each one had a harp and golden bowls full of incense—that’s the prayers of the saints, btw.
And they dropped a new track, singing: “You’re the one, ‘cause you got sacrificed and bought people for God with your blood—every tribe, every language, every people, every nation.”
“You made them royalty and priests for our God. They’re gonna run things on earth.”
Then I looked again and saw a whole squad of angels—millions on millions—circling the throne, the creatures, and the elders.
They were shouting loud: “Worthy is the Lamb who got murked—to grab power, riches, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and praise!”
Then I heard everything—in heaven, on earth, under the earth, in the sea—every creature saying: “To the One on the throne and to the Lamb: Blessing, honor, glory, and power—forever and ever!”
The four creatures said, “Facts.” The elders dropped low and worshipped.
Then I saw the Lamb crack open seal one. One of the four living creatures shouted like thunder, “Pull up!”
I looked—and boom, a white horse. Rider had a bow, got crowned, and rode out like, “I’m here to win.”
When he popped seal two, the second creature said, “Pull up!”
Another horse came—this one red and wild. Its rider got the OK to snatch peace from the earth, so people would turn on each other. He had a big blade.
Seal three? Cracked. Third creature said, “Pull up!” I saw a black horse. Rider had scales in hand.
I heard a voice from the creature squad say, “Wheat’s a day’s wage. Barley too. But don’t mess with the oil or the wine.”
Seal four? Cracked. Fourth creature said, “Pull up!”
I saw a pale horse. Rider’s name? Death. The Grave was tailing him. They got clearance to wipe out a fourth of the earth—sword, famine, plague, and wild beasts.
Seal five? Cracked. I saw under the altar the souls of those who got silenced for repping God’s Word and staying loyal.
They cried out, “How long, Lord—holy and true—till you drop justice on the ones who did us dirty?”
Each got a white robe and was told, “Rest a bit. More of your squad still gotta go through it like you did.”
Then the Lamb cracked seal six—and boom, a massive quake. Sun went blackout. Moon turned blood-red.
Stars started dropping like unpinned stories. Sky was glitching.
The sky peeled back like a scroll rolling up. Mountains and islands got moved like furniture.
Kings, bosses, generals, rich folks, the powerful, everyone—hid in caves and under rocks.
They yelled to the mountains, “Fall on us! Hide us from the face of the One on the throne and the Lamb’s wrath!”
“The big day of their wrath just hit. Who can even stand?”
After that, I saw four angels posted at earth’s corners, holding back the winds—no breeze hitting land, sea, or trees.
Then I saw another angel rising from the sunrise zone, holding the seal of the living God. He shouted to the four wind-holders, who had clearance to wreck the earth and sea:
“Hold up! Don’t touch the land, sea, or trees till we tag God’s servants with the seal—foreheads only.”
I heard the headcount of the sealed: 144,000. All from the tribes of Israel.
Tribe of Judah? 12K sealed. Reuben? 12K. Gad? 12K.
Asher? 12K. Naphtali? 12K. Manasseh? 12K.
Simeon? 12K. Levi? 12K. Issachar? 12K.
Zebulun? 12K. Joseph? 12K. Benjamin? 12K sealed.

After that, I looked—and boom, a massive crowd. Too many to count. Every nation, tribe, people, and language. Standing in front of the throne and the Lamb, rocking white fits and waving palm branches.
They shouted loud: “Salvation’s from our God on the throne—and the Lamb!”
All the angels were around the throne, the elders, and the four creatures. They dropped face-down and worshipped God.
Saying: “Amen! Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanks, honor, power, and strength—forever and ever. Amen!”
One of the elders asked me, “Who are these in white fits? Where’d they come from?”
I said, “Sir, you know.” He said, “These are the ones who made it through the big storm. They washed their robes in the Lamb’s blood—now they’re shining.”
“That’s why they’re posted in front of God’s throne, serving him day and night in his temple. And the One on the throne’s got them covered.”
“No more hunger. No more thirst. No sunburn. No heatstroke.”
“The Lamb at the center of the throne will be their shepherd. He’ll lead them to living water. And God will wipe every tear from their eyes.”
When the Lamb cracked seal seven, heaven went dead silent—for like half an hour. No sound. Just awe.
I saw the seven angels standing in front of God. Each got handed a trumpet—like, it’s go time.
Then another angel pulled up with a golden censer. He parked at the altar and got loaded with incense—plus all the prayers from the saints. Straight to the throne.
The incense smoke, mixed with the saints’ prayers, floated up from the angel’s hand to God. Holy aroma.
Then the angel grabbed the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and launched it at the earth. Thunder cracked. Lightning flashed. Earth shook. It was on.
The seven trumpet angels lined up, ready to blow.
First trumpet: hail and fire mixed with blood got launched. Burned a third of the earth, trees, and all the green grass. Nature took a hit.
Second trumpet: something like a blazing mountain got yeeted into the sea. A third of the ocean turned blood-red.
A third of sea life died. A third of ships wrecked. Maritime chaos.
Third trumpet: a massive star, burning like a torch, dropped from the sky. Landed on a third of the rivers and springs.
The star’s name? Wormwood. It turned the waters bitter. People drank it and got clapped—water was toxic.
Fourth trumpet: a third of the sun, moon, and stars got dimmed. Daylight lost a third. Night too. Cosmic blackout.
Then I looked and saw a solo eagle flying midair, yelling loud: “Woe! Woe! Woe to the people still on earth—‘cause the next three trumpet blasts are gonna hit different.”
Fifth trumpet hit. I saw a star that had already dropped from the sky. He got handed the key to the abyss trapdoor.
He popped it open—and smoke blasted out like a furnace. Sun and sky got blacked out from the smoke cloud.
Out of the smoke came these wild locusts, but not normal ones. They got power like scorpions, ready to sting.
They weren’t allowed to touch the grass, trees, or plants—just people who didn’t have God’s seal on their foreheads.
They couldn’t kill, only torture for five months. The pain hit like a scorpion sting—straight agony.
In those days, people will be begging to die, but death won’t pick up. They’ll chase it, but it’ll ghost them.
The locusts looked like war horses, prepped for battle. They had gold-like crowns, human-ish faces,
hair like long waves, teeth like lions, and
armor like iron plates. Their wings sounded like a stampede of chariots charging into war.
They had tails like scorpions, with stingers locked and loaded. Five months of pain was their mission.
Their boss? The angel of the abyss. Hebrew name: Abaddon. Greek name: Apollyon. Both mean “Destroyer.”
First “woe” just passed. Two more loading.
Sixth trumpet hit. I heard a voice from the golden altar in front of God.
It told the sixth trumpet angel, “Unleash the four chained-up angels at the big river Euphrates.”
The four angels—prepped for this exact hour, day, month, and year—got released to wipe out a third of humanity.
The cavalry squad they led? Two hundred million deep. I heard the number loud and clear.
Here’s what I saw: horses decked out in fire-red, blue, and sulfur-yellow armor. Their riders had lion heads breathing fire, smoke, and burning sulfur.
That fire, smoke, and sulfur? Took out a third of humanity. Straight judgment.
The horses’ power was in their mouths and tails. Their tails were like snakes with heads—biting and striking.
But the rest of the people who didn’t get clapped? Still didn’t flip. They kept chasing idols—gold, silver, bronze, stone, wood—stuff that can’t see, hear, or move.
They didn’t bounce from their murders, dark arts, hookup culture, or thefts. No repentance. Just vibes and violence.
Then I saw another angel—massive, shining. Came down from the sky, wrapped in a cloud, rainbow over his head, face glowing like the sun, legs like fire pillars.
He had a little scroll in his hand—already open. He planted one foot on the sea, one on land, like “I run this.”
Then he shouted loud—like a lion mid-roar. When he did, seven thunders answered back with their own voices.
I was about to write down what the thunders said, but a voice from heaven said, “Nah, seal that up. Don’t write it.”
The angel standing on sea and land raised his right hand to the sky,
and swore by the One who lives forever—the one who made the sky, earth, sea, and everything in them—saying, “No more delay.”
“When the seventh angel blows the trumpet, the mystery of God will be unlocked—just like he told his prophets.”
Then the voice from heaven spoke to me again: “Go grab the open scroll from the angel standing on sea and land.”
So I pulled up to the angel and said, “Let me get that scroll.” He said, “Take it and eat it. It'll taste sweet going down, but your stomach’s gonna feel it.”
I took the scroll and ate it. Tasted sweet like honey—but once it hit my gut, it turned bitter.
Then I was told, “You still got more to say—about nations, languages, kings, and the whole world.”
I got handed a measuring rod—looked like a staff. Voice said, “Go measure God’s temple, the altar, and the ones worshipping there.”
“But skip the outer court—it’s for the outsiders. They’ll trample the holy city for 42 months.”
“I’m sending my two witnesses. They’ll speak truth for 1,260 days, dressed in sack drip.”
These two? They’re the two olive trees and lampstands standing in front of the Lord of the earth.
If anyone tries to mess with them, fire comes out their mouths and fries the ops. That’s how their enemies get clapped.
They’ve got power to shut the sky—no rain while they’re speaking. They can flip water into blood and drop plagues whenever they want. Full control.
When their mission’s done, the beast from the abyss will rise up, go full aggro, and take them out.
Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city—spiritually called Sodom and Egypt—where their Lord got crucified.
People from every tribe, language, and nation will stare at their bodies for three and a half days. No one lets them get buried.
The world will throw a party—celebrating, sending gifts—‘cause those two prophets had been a problem.
But after three and a half days, God’s breath hit them—they stood up. Everyone watching? Shook.
Then they heard a loud voice from heaven: “Come up here.” They ascended in a cloud while their haters watched.
That hour, a massive quake hit. A tenth of the city collapsed. Seven thousand people died. The rest were terrified and gave props to God.
Second “woe” just passed. Third one’s pulling up fast.
Seventh trumpet hit. Loud voices in heaven shouted: “Kingdoms of this world just got claimed by our Lord and his Christ. He’s gonna reign forever.”
The twenty-four elders, seated before God, dropped face-down and worshipped.
Saying, “We thank you, Lord God Almighty—who is and was—‘cause you flexed your power and took the throne.”

“The nations raged, but your wrath hit. Time’s up—for the dead to get judged, for your servants to get rewarded—prophets, saints, and all who repped your name. And time to destroy the destroyers of the earth.”
Then God’s temple in heaven opened. The ark of his covenant was visible inside. Lightning cracked, thunder rolled, earth shook, and hail came down hard.
And there popped up a wild sign in the sky; a woman, glowing like the sun, moon under her feet, and a crown of twelve stars on her head:
and she was pregnant, crying out in labor, in pain, ready to push.
And another sign showed up in the sky; a massive red dragon, seven heads, ten horns, and seven crowns stacked on those heads.
And his tail whipped a third of the stars and flung them to earth: and the dragon parked himself in front of the woman, waiting to snatch her baby the second it dropped.
And she gave birth to a boy—destined to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her baby got snatched up to God, and to his throne.
And the woman dipped into the wilderness, where God had a safe zone set up for her, to keep her fed for 1,260 days.
And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels threw hands with the dragon; and the dragon and his squad clapped back.
And they lost—couldn’t hold their ground; neither was there space for them in heaven anymore.
And the big dragon got booted—the old serpent, aka the Devil, aka Satan, the one who scams the whole world: he got tossed to earth, and his angels with him.

And I heard a loud voice in heaven say, “Now salvation, power, kingdom, and the authority of Christ just hit: ‘cause the accuser of our fam—who kept dragging us before God day and night—is finally canceled.”
And they beat him by the Lamb’s blood, and by their testimony; and they didn’t fold, even when it cost them their lives.
Therefore, flex up, you heavens, and everyone chilling there. But woe to the earth and sea! ‘Cause the devil just pulled up to y’all, heated, knowing his time’s almost up.
And when the dragon saw he got dropped to earth, he went full rage mode on the woman who birthed the male child.

And the woman got two wings like a giant eagle, so she could fly to her wilderness hideout, her God-made safe zone, where she’d get fed for a time, and times, and half a time, far from the serpent’s reach.
And the serpent spit water like a flood out his mouth after the woman, trying to sweep her away.
And the earth came through for her: opened up and swallowed the flood the dragon spit out.
And the dragon was big mad at the woman, and went to war with the rest of her kids—those who keep God’s commands, and hold tight to Jesus’ receipts.
And I stood on the beach, watching; and I saw a beast rise out the sea, with seven heads and ten horns, ten crowns on the horns, and wild names on the heads.
And the beast I saw looked like a leopard, feet like a bear’s, mouth like a lion’s: and the dragon gave him his power, his throne, and full authority.
And I saw one of his heads looking like it got clapped—fatal wound—but it healed up: and the whole world was like, “Whoa,” and followed the beast.
And they worshipped the dragon for giving the beast power: and they worshipped the beast too, saying, “Who’s like this beast? Who can even fight him?”
And he was given a mouth to talk big and blaspheme; and power to run his mouth for forty-two months.
And he opened his mouth to drag God’s name, his tabernacle, and everyone chilling in heaven.
And he was allowed to go to war with the saints, and win: and power was given him over every tribe, language, and nation.
And all who live on earth will worship him, whose names aren’t in the Lamb’s Book of Life—the Lamb who was slain from the world’s foundation.
If you got ears, listen up.
Anyone meant for captivity? Off they go: anyone meant to get clapped by the sword? That’s how it’ll go down. This is where the saints need patience and faith.
And I saw another beast coming up out the earth; he had two horns like a lamb, but talked like the dragon.
And he flexed all the authority of the first beast in his presence, and made the earth and everyone on it worship the first beast—yeah, the one who bounced back from the death wound.
And he pulled off wild signs, even made fire drop from the sky to earth in front of people.
And he scammed those living on earth with the signs he was allowed to do in front of the beast; saying to the people, “Build a statue for the beast who got stabbed and lived.”
And he was allowed to give breath to the statue, so it could speak, and even cause anyone who didn’t worship it to get clapped.
And he made everyone—small and great, rich and broke, free and slave—get marked on their right hand, or forehead:
and no one could buy or sell unless they had the mark, or the beast’s name, or the number of his name.
Here’s where wisdom kicks in. Let the one with insight count the beast’s number: for it’s the number of a man; and his number is six hundred sixty-six.
And I looked, and there was the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000—tagged with his name and his Father’s name on their foreheads.
And I heard a voice from heaven, like a waterfall, like thunder, like a whole band playing: and the sound I heard was like harpers shredding on their harps:
and they sang a new anthem in front of the throne, the four creatures, and the elders: and no one could learn that song except the 144,000, who got redeemed from the earth.
These are the ones who didn’t fold to hookup culture—they stayed loyal. They follow the Lamb wherever he goes. They were bought out early, firstfruits to God and the Lamb.
And in their mouth was no cap: they were flawless.
And I saw another angel flying midair, with the eternal gospel to drop on everyone—nations, tribes, languages, and people,
saying loud, “Fear God, and give him glory; ‘cause the hour of his judgment just hit: worship the one who made the sky, earth, sea, and water springs.”
And another angel followed, saying, “Babylon’s done! The great city’s fallen—she made all nations drink her toxic hookup wine.”
And a third angel followed them, shouting, “If anyone worships the beast and his statue, and takes his mark on their forehead or hand,
they’ll drink the full cup of God’s wrath—no chaser. They’ll get torched with fire and sulfur in front of the holy angels and the Lamb:
and the smoke of their torment rises forever: no rest, day or night, for those who worship the beast and his image, or take his mark.”
Here’s where the saints flex their patience: the ones who keep God’s commands and stay loyal to Jesus.
And I heard a voice from heaven say, “Write this: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.” “Yeah,” says the Spirit, “they can rest now; their grind follows them.”
And I looked, and saw a white cloud, and someone sitting on it like the Son of man, with a gold crown and a sharp sickle in hand.
And another angel came out of the temple, shouting to the one on the cloud, “Swing your sickle, it’s harvest time; the earth’s crop is ripe.”
And the one on the cloud swung his sickle, and the earth got harvested.
And another angel came out of the temple in heaven, also holding a sharp sickle.
And another angel came from the altar—he had fire power—and shouted to the one with the sharp sickle, “Swing it! Cut the grape clusters from the earth’s vine; they’re fully ripe.”
And the angel swung his sickle, harvested the grapes, and tossed them into the great winepress of God’s wrath.
And the winepress got stomped outside the city, and blood poured out like a flood—rising to the horses’ bridles, stretching 1,600 furlongs.
And I saw another sign in heaven, big and wild—seven angels with seven last plagues; ‘cause with them, God’s wrath hits full send.
And I saw something like a sea of glass, mixed with fire: and the ones who beat the beast, his image, his mark, and his name’s number were standing on that sea of glass, holding God’s harps.
And they dropped the song of Moses—the servant of God—and the song of the Lamb, saying, “Great and awesome are your works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are your ways, King of saints.”
“Who won’t fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? You alone are holy: all nations will pull up and worship; ‘cause your judgments just got revealed.”
And after that, I looked, and the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven opened up:
and the seven angels with the seven plagues came out of the temple, dressed in pure white linen, golden sashes across their chests.
And one of the four living creatures handed the seven angels seven golden bowls, full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.
And the temple filled with smoke from God’s glory and power; and no one could enter till the seven plagues from the seven angels were finished.
And I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, “Go—pour out the seven bowls of God’s wrath on the earth.”
And the first went, and dumped his bowl on the land; and a nasty, painful sore broke out on the people who had the beast’s mark, and worshipped his image.
And the second angel poured his bowl into the sea; and it turned into blood, thick like a corpse’s—every living thing in the sea died.
And the third angel poured his bowl into the rivers and springs; and they turned into blood.
And I heard the angel of the waters say, “You’re righteous, Lord, who is, and was, and shall be, ‘cause you judged like this:
for they shed the blood of saints and prophets, and now you gave them blood to drink—they earned it.”
And I heard another voice from the altar say, “True that, Lord God Almighty, your judgments are right and just.”
And the fourth angel poured his bowl on the sun; and it was given power to scorch people with fire.
And people got burned bad, and cursed God’s name—he had power over those plagues—but they still didn’t repent or give him glory.
And the fifth angel poured his bowl on the beast’s throne; and his whole kingdom went dark. People chewed their tongues in pain,
and cursed the God of heaven because of their pain and sores, and still didn’t repent of their actions.
And the sixth angel poured his bowl on the great river Euphrates; and its water dried up, making way for the kings from the east.
And I saw three unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet.
For they’re demon spirits, doing signs, going out to the kings of the world to gather them for the big war on the great day of God Almighty.
“Look, I come like a thief. Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps their clothes on, so they don’t walk around exposed and get clowned.”
And they gathered them at a place called in Hebrew, Armageddon.
And the seventh angel poured his bowl into the air; and a loud voice came from the throne in the temple, saying, “It is done.”
And there were flashes, rumbles, thunder, and a quake so massive—no quake like it had ever hit before.
And the great city split into three parts, and the cities of the nations collapsed: and great Babylon got remembered before God, to get the full cup of his wrath.
And every island dipped, and the mountains vanished.
And giant hailstones—each one like a hundred pounds—dropped from the sky on people: and they cursed God because the hail was brutal. It hit hard.
And one of the seven bowl angels pulled up and said to me, “Come here; I’ll show you the judgment of the great prostitute who’s posted on many waters:
with whom the kings of the earth hooked up, and the people got drunk off her scandalous wine.”
So he carried me away in the Spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet beast, full of blasphemous names, with seven heads and ten horns.
And the woman was dripped out in purple and scarlet, iced with gold, gems, and pearls, holding a gold cup full of filth and her hookup energy:
and on her forehead was a name written—mystery style: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF EARTH’S FILTH.
And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of Jesus’ martyrs: and when I saw her, I was shook—mad amazed.
And the angel said, “Why you shook? I’ll break it down—the mystery of the woman, and the beast she’s riding, the one with seven heads and ten horns.”

“The beast you saw was, and is not; and is about to rise from the abyss, and head straight into destruction: and the people on earth whose names aren’t in the Book of Life—written from the world’s start—will be stunned when they see the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.”
“Here’s where you need brainpower. The seven heads? They’re seven mountains the woman’s sitting on:
and they’re also seven kings: five are gone, one’s alive, and the last hasn’t shown up yet; and when he does, he won’t last long.”
“And the beast that was, and is not, is the eighth—he’s one of the seven, but he’s headed for destruction.”
“The ten horns you saw? Ten kings who haven’t gotten crowns yet, but they’ll get power for one hour with the beast.”
“They’re all in sync—same mindset—and they hand over their power and authority to the beast.”
“They’ll go to war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will clap them: ‘cause he’s Lord of lords, King of kings—and the ones rolling with him are the called, chosen, and faithful.”
And he said to me, “The waters you saw, where the prostitute sits? That’s people, crowds, nations, and languages.”
“And the ten horns and the beast you saw—they’ll turn on the prostitute, strip her, wreck her, eat her up, and burn her down.”
“For God put it in their hearts to carry out his plan, to unite and hand their kingdom to the beast, until God’s words are fully played out.”
“And the woman you saw? She’s the big city that runs the kings of the earth.”
And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, with major authority; and the earth lit up with his glory.
And he cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and has become a demon hangout, a haunt for every unclean spirit, every nasty bird, and every cursed beast.”
“For all nations drank the wine of her wild hookups, the kings of the earth linked up with her, and the merchants got rich off her luxury addiction.”
And I heard another voice from heaven say, “Come out of her, my people, so you don’t get caught in her sins, and don’t take the hit when judgment drops.”
“For her sins stacked up to heaven, and God remembered all her dirty deeds.”
“Pay her back double for what she did: double the pain, double the cup she poured out—give it back to her.”
“As much as she flexed and lived it up, give her that much torment and grief: ‘cause she said in her heart, ‘I sit as queen, I’m no widow, I’ll never see sorrow.’”
“So in one day, her plagues will hit—death, mourning, and famine; and she’ll get burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judges her.”
And the kings of the earth who hooked up with her and lived large will cry and mourn over her, when they see the smoke of her burning,
standing far off, scared of her torment, saying, “Whoa, whoa, that great city Babylon, the strong one! In one hour your judgment came.”
And the merchants of the earth will cry and mourn over her; ‘cause nobody’s buying their goods anymore:
gold, silver, gems, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, scarlet, all kinds of scented wood, ivory, expensive stuff, bronze, iron, marble,
cinnamon, incense, perfume, myrrh, wine, oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, and even human lives and souls.
“And the fruit your soul craved is gone from you, and all your luxury and shine is gone—you’ll never get it back.”
The merchants who sold those things and got rich from her will stand far off, scared of her torment, crying and mourning,
saying, “Whoa, whoa, that great city, dressed in fine linen, purple and scarlet, iced out in gold, gems, and pearls!”
“In one hour, all that wealth got wrecked.” And every ship captain, sailor, and sea trader stood far off,
and cried when they saw the smoke from her fire, saying, “What city was ever like this one?”
And they threw dust on their heads, crying and mourning, shouting, “Whoa, whoa, that great city, where all who had ships got rich by her hustle! In one hour, she’s toast.”
“Rejoice over her, heaven, and you saints, apostles, and prophets; ‘cause God just clapped her for what she did to you.”
And a mighty angel picked up a boulder like a giant millstone, and threw it into the sea, saying, “That’s how Babylon the great city will get thrown down—fast and final.”
“No more music in you—no harps, singers, flutes, or trumpets. No more craftsmen. No more grinding mills.”
“No more light in your windows. No more wedding vibes. Your merchants were the world’s elites, and your sorcery fooled all nations.”
And in her was found the blood of prophets, saints, and everyone who got slain on earth.
And after these things I heard a loud squad in heaven shouting, “Hallelujah! Salvation, glory, and power belong to our God:
for his judgments are true and just: he judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her hookups, and avenged the blood of his servants on her.”
And again they said, “Hallelujah!” And her smoke rose up forever and ever.
And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures dropped face-down and worshipped God who sat on the throne, saying, “Amen; Hallelujah.”
And a voice came out of the throne, saying, “Praise our God, all you his servants, and you who fear him, both small and great.”
And I heard what sounded like a massive crowd, like rushing water, like thunder rolling, saying, “Hallelujah! For the Lord God Almighty reigns.”
“Let’s rejoice and be glad, and give him glory: for the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride made herself ready.”
And she was given fine linen to wear, clean and bright: for the fine linen is the righteousness of the saints.
And he said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” And he added, “These are the true words of God.”

And I dropped to my knees at his feet to worship him. But he said, “Don’t do that: I’m your fellow servant, and of your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus: worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
And I saw heaven open, and there was a white horse; and the one riding it was called Faithful and True, and he judges and makes war in righteousness.
His eyes were flames of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written that no one knew but himself.
And he was clothed in a robe dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.
And the armies of heaven followed him on white horses, dressed in fine linen, white and clean.
And out of his mouth came a sharp sword, to strike the nations: and he’ll rule them with a rod of iron: and he stomps the winepress of the fury of Almighty God.
And on his robe and thigh was a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.
And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he shouted to all the birds flying midair, “Come, gather for the great supper of God;
so you can eat the flesh of kings, captains, mighty men, horses and riders, and everyone else—free and slave, small and great.”
And I saw the beast, the kings of the earth, and their armies gathered to fight the one on the horse and his army.

And the beast was captured, and with him the false prophet who did signs in his presence—scamming people into taking the mark and worshipping the image. Both were thrown alive into the lake of fire burning with sulfur.
And the rest were clapped by the sword from the rider’s mouth: and all the birds feasted on their flesh.
And I saw an angel come down from heaven, holding the key to the abyss and a big chain in his hand.
And he grabbed the dragon—that old serpent, the Devil, aka Satan—and chained him up for a thousand years,
and threw him into the abyss, locked it, and sealed it shut, so he couldn’t scam the nations anymore till the thousand years were up: after that, he’s getting released for a short run.

And I saw thrones, and people sitting on them, with judgment authority given to them: and I saw the souls of those who got executed for repping Jesus and God’s Word, who didn’t worship the beast or his image, and didn’t take the mark on their foreheads or hands; and they came back to life, and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
(The rest of the dead didn’t come back to life till the thousand years were finished.) This is the first resurrection.
Blessed and holy is the one who’s in on the first resurrection: the second death has no power over them, but they’ll be priests of God and Christ, and reign with him a thousand years.
And when the thousand years are up, Satan will get released from his prison,
and he’ll go out to scam the nations in the four corners of the earth—Gog and Magog—to gather them for battle: their squad is massive, like the sand on the beach.
And they marched across the earth, surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and torched them.
And the devil who scammed them got tossed into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet already were, and they’ll be tormented day and night forever.
And I saw a great white throne, and the One sitting on it, from whose face the earth and sky dipped—and no place was found for them.

And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the Book of Life: and the dead were judged out of what was written in the books, based on what they did.
And the sea gave up the dead in it; and death and the grave gave up the dead in them: and everyone got judged based on what they did.
And death and the grave were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
And anyone whose name wasn’t found in the Book of Life got tossed into the lake of fire.
And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth had dipped; and the sea was gone too.
And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, dressed like a bride ready for her wedding.
And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, “Look, God’s home is now with humanity, and he’ll live with them: they’ll be his people, and God himself will be with them, and be their God.”
And God will wipe every tear from their eyes; no more death, no sorrow, no crying, no pain: the old order is gone.
And the one sitting on the throne said, “Look, I’m making everything new.” And he said, “Write this down: these words are true and faithful.”
And he said to me, “It is done. I’m Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I’ll give water freely from the spring of life to anyone who’s thirsty.”
“Whoever overcomes will inherit all this; and I’ll be their God, and they’ll be my child.”
“But the cowardly, unfaithful, corrupt, murderers, sexually wild, sorcerers, idol worshippers, and all liars—they’re headed for the lake burning with fire and sulfur: that’s the second death.”
And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the last plagues came and said, “Come, I’ll show you the Bride, the Lamb’s wife.”
And he carried me away in the Spirit to a high mountain, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God,
shining with God’s glory: its light was like a rare jewel, clear like crystal.
It had a massive, high wall with twelve gates, and twelve angels at the gates, and names written on them—the twelve tribes of Israel:
three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south, and three on the west.
And the city wall had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
And the angel who talked with me had a gold measuring rod to measure the city, its gates, and its wall.
And the city was laid out square—same length and width: and he measured it—12,000 furlongs each way. It was just as tall as it was wide and long.
And he measured the wall—144 cubits thick, by human scale (which the angel was using).
The wall was built of jasper: and the city was pure gold, clear like glass.
The foundations of the wall were decorated with every kind of gem: first jasper, second sapphire, third chalcedony, fourth emerald,
fifth sardonyx, sixth sardius, seventh chrysolite, eighth beryl, ninth topaz, tenth chrysoprase, eleventh jacinth, twelfth amethyst.
And the twelve gates were twelve pearls—each gate made from a single pearl: and the main street was pure gold, clear like glass.
And I didn’t see a temple in the city: ‘cause the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.
And the city didn’t need sun or moon to shine on it: ‘cause God’s glory lit it up, and the Lamb was its lamp.
And the nations will walk in its light: and the kings of the earth will bring their glory into it.
And its gates will never shut by day: and there’s no night there.
And they’ll bring the glory and honor of the nations into it.
And nothing unclean will ever enter it, nor anyone who does shady or fake stuff: only those written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.
And he showed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
In the middle of the street, and on both sides of the river, was the tree of life, dropping twelve kinds of fruit—one for each month: and the leaves were for healing the nations.
And there’ll be no more curse: but the throne of God and the Lamb will be in it; and his servants will serve him:
and they’ll see his face; and his name will be on their foreheads.
And there’ll be no night there; no need for lamps or sunlight; for the Lord God lights them up: and they’ll reign forever and ever.
And he said to me, “These words are faithful and true: and the Lord God of the holy prophets sent his angel to show his servants what must soon go down.”
“Look, I come quickly: blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this scroll.”
And I, John, saw and heard these things. And when I heard and saw, I dropped to worship at the feet of the angel who showed me all this.
Then he said, “Don’t do that: I’m your fellow servant, and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep this scroll. Worship God.”
And he said to me, “Don’t seal the words of this prophecy: the time is near.”
“Let the one who’s unjust stay unjust: the dirty stay dirty: the righteous stay righteous: and the holy stay holy.”
“And look, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to pay everyone based on what they’ve done.”
“I’m Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.”
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so they can access the tree of life, and enter the city through the gates.
Outside are the dogs, sorcerers, the wild ones, murderers, idolaters, and everyone who loves and lives in lies.
“I, Jesus, sent my angel to testify these things to you for the churches. I’m the Root and Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.”
And the Spirit and the bride say, “Come.” And let the one who hears say, “Come.” And let the one who’s thirsty come. And whoever wants—let them take the water of life freely.
For I testify to everyone who hears the words of this prophecy: if anyone adds to it, God will add to them the plagues written in this scroll:
and if anyone deletes from the words of this prophecy, God will take away their share of the tree of life, and the holy city, written in this scroll.
He who testifies these things says, “Surely I come quickly.” Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
